posts.text:
Few money questions start more arguments than this one: is renting really "dead money"? So I ran the numbers.

I modelled renting vs buying the same home in all 12 UK regions and 316 local areas, with a backtest to 2005.

What I found:

- Mortgage interest is "dead money" too. In year one it is 77% to 107% of the rent on the same home.
- If house prices keep rising 3% a year, buying wins after 1.4 to 4.1 years.
- If prices stay flat, it takes 11 to 30+ years.
- In Newcastle, buying wins within a year. In Elmbridge, Waverley and Mole Valley, it never does within 30 years.

So the honest answer: renting isn't dead money, and buying isn't a sure thing. It is a bet on house prices.

The full analysis, the data and the Python and R code are free on my site, Truth with Data, with a calculator for your own area. Links in the first comment.

Where in the UK do you think buying makes least sense?

posts.text:
Everyone has an opinion on which jobs AI is replacing. I wanted data.

I matched AI usage scores for 722 US occupations (Anthropic's Economic Index) to official employment figures from 2019 to 2025.

The correlation between how exposed a job is to AI and how its employment changed: r = 0.01.

Not a typo. Across whole occupations, exposure barely predicts what happened, and the same pattern was there before ChatGPT.

Where displacement does show up: customer service reps, office clerks, receptionists, medical transcriptionists, technical writers, interpreters and graphic designers.

And the headline case cuts both ways: computer programmers fell 54%, but were already down 31% before ChatGPT. Software developers grew 33%.

Exposure isn't replacement. Not yet, and not across whole occupations.

The method, a placebo test, the data and code, and a free tool to look up your own job are on Truth with Data. Links in the comments.

Too early to see it, or overhyped?

posts.text:
The most expensive statistics mistake I see in business teams: checking an A/B test every day and stopping it the moment it looks significant.

So I simulated it. 10,000 A/B tests where both versions were identical, so any "winner" is pure noise.

- Check once, at the planned end: 5% false winners, as promised.
- Check weekly: 11%.
- Check daily and stop at the first p < 0.05: 25%.

One in four "winning" changes did nothing at all.

Three fixes:
1. Decide the sample size before you start, and don't stop early.
2. If you must monitor, use a method built for it, such as sequential testing.
3. Report the confidence interval, not just "significant: yes".

The full guide (with Python and R code) and a free sample size calculator are on Truth with Data. Links in the comments.

Have you seen a "winning" test fall apart after launch?

posts.title: Owning vs renting the same average home in every UK region: monthly costs in the first year (2026)
posts.first_comment:
What this shows: for the average home in each UK region, the unrecoverable monthly cost of owning it in the first year with a 10% deposit (mortgage interest, maintenance, buildings insurance, and the return the deposit could have earned), against the rent on the same home. Capital repayment isn't counted because it becomes equity.

- Mortgage interest alone is 77% to 107% of the rent. In the East Midlands, West Midlands, East of England, South East and Wales it is more than the rent.
- Add the other costs and owning is more expensive than renting in all 12 regions.
- Buying only gets ahead through house-price growth. At 3% a year (the 2005 to 2026 pace) it wins after 1.4 years (Scotland) to 4.1 years (South East). If prices stay flat it takes 11 years to more than 30.

Data: HM Land Registry UK House Price Index (July 2026), ONS Price Index of Private Rents, Bank of England quoted mortgage rates. Made with Python (pandas, matplotlib); the model is cross-checked in R.

Full write-up, method and code: https://truthwithdata.com/blog/is-renting-dead-money-uk.html?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=2026-11-08-rd-profile-rent-vs-buy

Calculator for your own numbers: https://truthwithdata.com/tools/rent-vs-buy-calculator.html?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=2026-11-08-rd-profile-rent-vs-buy
